title: Flower patch
summary: A patch of wild flowers: the part of a plant that makes seeds, and a meeting place for insects.

layers.basics: A flower is how many plants reproduce. The coloured petals and the scent advertise to insects. A visiting bee collects sugary nectar and sticky pollen, and carries pollen from flower to flower, which lets the plants make seeds.
layers.deeper: Pollen carries the plant's male cells; the part of the flower that receives it leads to the seed. When an insect moves pollen between flowers of the same kind, that is pollination. Close-up, the leaf and stem surfaces are covered in tiny pores and hairs.
layers.expert: Flowering plants (angiosperms) are the largest group of land plants. The close-up here shows a generic leaf surface, not the flowers drawn. The park is a simplified scene, not a scan of a real place.

facts: 16 flowers in one patch (a simplified model)
